text:
michael: Heads-up - we've started seeing GPU P2P failures on several Ampere hosts after the kernel + NVIDIA driver push last night. Affected nodes: ampr-usc-*/ampr-euw-* in west/us-east/eu-west. Latency for multi-gpu jobs jumped and NCCL reports fallbacks to PCIe copies.

sara: Ugh, saw that on ampr-usc-12 too. NCCL logs show `P2P disabled` and I can repro with a small test. Suspect PCIe ACS or BAR1 mapping changed with the new driver/kernel combo. :face_with_raised_eyebrow:

ben: Confirmed on my end. Quick grep from one host:

```
$ dmesg | tail -n 40
[  112.345678] nvidia: module 530.41 loaded
[  112.346010] pcieport 0000:00:1c.0: ACS: enabled
[  112.346200] pci 0000:65:00.0: BAR 1: 256M assigned
```

But when I run the NCCL test we get `ncclP2pSupport=false` and it falls back to intra-node copies over host memory.

kelsey: That BAR1 sizing is interesting — older nodes had BAR1=512M. If the driver/kernel combo changed BAR sizing heuristics, some GPUs might not export full MMIO windows, causing P2P to fail. Could be the kernel's `pcie_fr` or ACS handling.

michael: Ops-bot shows the canary rollout succeeded but the full rollout continued. @ops-bot which hosts were canaries?

ops-bot: Deployment canary group: ampr-usc-2, ampr-euw-1, ampr-use-5. Canary success: 3/3 (health checks green). Full rollout: started 1771998000, 60% complete when alerts started.

sara: Canary checks only ran basic GPU health and driver module load. They didn't run NCCL P2P tests. We need better canary validation for multi-gpu kernels.

ben: Impact summary so far: ~18% of Ampere fleet that upgraded shows P2P disabled on at least one GPU pair, causing 2-3x latency on distributed inference and training. Some dedicated clusters are hitting capacity because we cordoned failing nodes (we're at ~82% capacity in west-us).

kelsey: For mitigation I propose:
- Rollback driver on dedicated clusters in west-us and eu to previous stable (530.30 -> 525.x) for nodes with high P2P failure rates.
- Add an NCCL P2P smoke test to canary pipeline. Example command:
```
nccl-tests/build/all_reduce_perf -b 8 -e 32M -f 2 -g 2
```
- Temporarily tag affected racks and route multi-gpu workloads away via scheduler policy.

michael: Agreed. @sara can you coordinate the rollback runbook? Start with a small controlled rollback (10 nodes) and validate with the smoke test before expanding. Also file a vendor ticket with NVIDIA, include `dmesg`, `lspci -vv` and `nvidia-smi topo --matrix` outputs.

sara: On it. I'll start rollback on ampr-usc-2 as a test. Uploading logs to ticket: https://redwood.internal/tix/INF-3921

ben: Note: this will increase short-term cost because some jobs will be forced to remote hosts or queued. Ops should notify capacity planning and support to expect higher latency for customers on affected clusters.

kelsey: Also check ACS override flags. If we can toggle ACS for specific PCIe switches we might restore P2P without full rollback, but that's risky across tenant hardware. Vendor input needed.

ops-bot: Incident ticket INF-3921 created, severity P2. Paging oncall: @michael @kelsey @sara

michael: I'll own the rollback. Plan: 10-node pilot -> smoke tests -> 50-node incremental -> full region. Target to finish west-us pilot in next 3 hours. Will post status updates here. :rocket:

ben: TL;DR — driver/kernel combo changed BAR1/ACS behavior; P2P often disabled -> NCCL falling back to PCIe copies -> higher latency and capacity pressure. Rollback + better canary tests are the short-term path. Long term we need regression tests for BAR1/ACS across kernels and drivers.

sara: Pilot started on ampr-usc-2 (1772004500). First smoke test passed on node 1/2. Updating ticket with results.

michael: Thanks. If vendor comes back with a patch we can try a controlled upgrade; until then let's freeze the rollout and notify platform customers with dedicated capacity. I'll draft the customer note.
